research_question: How does DAO governance work in practice, and how should a reader judge a vote?

research_brief.purpose: Explain proposal stages, delegation, quorum, and concentration, using one documented process and current research.
research_brief.audience: Token holders and readers assessing how decisions are made in a DAO.
research_brief.data_period: Uniswap governance documentation as updated April 2026; research published in 2026.
research_brief.scope_limitations: Uniswap is one example, not the norm. Research findings are associations. Vote tallies in the post are illustrative.

sources.title: Governance Process
sources.scope: Phases, thresholds, and timings of Uniswap governance
sources.method: Published governance rules, last updated April 2026
sources.limitations: One protocol; governance can change the rules

sources.title: Guide to Voting
sources.scope: How delegation and voting work for holders

sources.title: Vote Delegation and Conformity in DAO Governance
sources.publisher: Communications of the Association for Information Systems
sources.scope: Delegated voting power and conformity with the leading outcome
sources.method: Analysis of voting data from one leading DAO
sources.limitations: One DAO, not named in the abstract; in press

sources.title: Voting Biases in Decentralized Autonomous Organization (DAO) Governance
sources.scope: How choice features relate to voting-power share
sources.limitations: Preprint, not peer reviewed; associations, not causal effects

statistics.claim: Uniswap governance requires 10 million UNI voting for in a Temperature Check, 1 million UNI delegated to submit an on-chain proposal, and 40 million UNI in favor to pass.
statistics.limitations: One protocol; thresholds can be changed by governance

statistics.claim: A 2026 preprint found author-selected choices were associated with a 58.8% higher voting-power share, approval-oriented choices 27.1%, and first-listed choices 7.7%.
statistics.population: DAO proposal choices studied by the authors

competitors.title: Demystifying the DAO Governance Process
headings: Do existing DAOs achieve fairness decentralized governance?
Do existing DAOs offer sufficient governance process documentation?
Do existing proposals ensure consistency between descriptions and code?
competitors.covered_well: Measures technical governance risks across a large sample of DAOs.
competitors.gaps: Technical and academic; little on delegation, quorum, or participation for a general reader.

competitors.title: Designing a Governance System for DAO: a Checklist for Web3 Founders
headings: Pre-DAO and Post-DAO stages of a Web3 project
Elements comprising the decentralized governance of a Web3 project
Making proposals, voting, and making decisions
competitors.covered_well: A founder's checklist for setting up governance and its legal wrapper.
competitors.gaps: Written for founders; minimal on delegation, quorum, or concentration of voting power.

competitors.title: DAO Governance Models: What You Need to Know
headings: How to Choose the Right DAO Governance Model
coverage: Token-weighted, quadratic, reputation, multi-signature, and hybrid models
sources: Named DAO examples; no research cited
competitors.covered_well: Explains five governance models with pros, cons, and examples.
competitors.gaps: No participation data, quorum mechanics, or measured concentration of voting power.

competitors.title: Building and Running a DAO: Why Governance Matters
headings: Experiments paved way for modern DAOs
competitors.covered_well: Sets out what governance has to manage and how DAOs organize to do it.
competitors.gaps: Dated 2021 and written by an investor in the sector; little on delegation, quorum, or participation rates.

competitors.title: Governance Tokens: How DAO Voting Works
headings: Benefits and Challenges of Token Governance
competitors.covered_well: Explains how governance tokens carry votes, with named protocol examples.
competitors.gaps: Names whale dominance and apathy without thresholds, quorum mechanics, or measured participation.

content_gaps: Ranking pages define DAOs or list governance models; few show real thresholds.
Turnout is quoted without saying what it is a share of.
Concentration among delegates is named but not shown.
Recent research on delegation behavior is absent from the explainers.
value_add: A documented process with its real thresholds, a way to read turnout and concentration, and two current studies described with their limits.

plan.reader_title: DAO Governance and DeFi: What Token Voting Controls
plan.seo_title: DAO Governance: How Token Voting Works in Practice
plan.meta_description: Learn how DAO governance works, how delegation and quorum shape voting power, and what token holders control in protocols such as Uniswap.
